mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate above 6% signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 YoY < -2% and UNRATE > 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >0.4pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE rises by >0.4pp for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline of at least 1% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenues and profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month by >1% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of >1% monthly INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase of at least 2% in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a decline of at least 0.5% in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a slowdown in economic activity and negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous month by >2% AND GDPC1 < previous month by >0.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS rises >2% and GDPC1 falls >0.5% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 2% for more than six consecutive months in a low-inflation environment (CPIAUCSL < 2% YoY) signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS < 2% for >6 months and CPIAUCSL < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment increase (PAYEMS) below 50,000 for three consecutive months signals persistent labor market weakness, which depresses consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS < 50,000 for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of at least 1% in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month by >1% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during four consecutive months of >1% monthly HOUST increases.
